epistemic.reason: The HFT's exact Arabic anchors and word indices match the supplied duration, measure, and counting tokens, but the scale-dislocation reading is a reconstructed legacy inference.

findings.title: The opening can be an unsealing of perception
findings.claim: Al-fatḥ can also carry an inward opening of understanding: faculties are granted without uptake, seeing and hearing arrive later, and belief adopted on the opening day no longer benefits its speakers.
findings.mechanism: The focus's knowledge-access facet meets exact HFT coordinates for hearing and sight in 32:9, belated seeing/hearing and certainty in 32:12, unheeded hearing/sight questions in 32:26-27, and belief with no benefit in 32:29. Together these moves make the opening an unveiling whose recognition comes too late.
findings.reader_payoff: The event is newly perceptible as forced recognition as well as an external proof or judgment.
findings.containment: The HFT source itself leaves open that changed perception is a consequence of an external judicial or victorious opening. This reading does not make al-fatḥ only an inward event or displace the other live senses.

epistemic.reason: Every coordinate is present in exact Arabic anchor evidence and matches its supplied root/token, but the inward-unsealing synthesis is legacy-unbound inference.

findings.mechanism: The focus truth root's fulfillment branch meets HFT-attributed acts of doing, repair, restraint, certainty, and belief across the surah. Their repeated before/after contrast changes truth from prediction alone into timely perception and enacted commitment.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus challenge turns back toward what truth costs in a life and whether its response came before the deadline.
findings.containment: Prediction remains a valid narrower reading, and ordinary truthful speech remains intact. The costly-transfer nomination is separate and is not collapsed into this action sequence.

epistemic.reason: Exact HFT anchors and word indices support each context role, while the move from those roles to a timed-action criterion is the reader's reconstructed inference.

findings.title: The opening is an asymmetric threshold
findings.claim: The focus opening can organize two opposed destinations: prepared reception for some and a failed exit with forced return for others. Its threshold is open in one direction and closed to revision in the other.
findings.mechanism: The focus physical-opening branch meets HFT-attributed prepared reception in 32:19 and enclosure, attempted exit, and forced return in 32:20. Their opposing movement changes the opening from common access into a threshold whose direction differs by party.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why an opening can mark both admission and the end of any useful return, without turning the noun into a synonym for closure.
findings.containment: This is an attributed contextual arrangement, not a claim that al-fatḥ lexically means a closed gate. The HFT source calls the threshold paradoxical; the focus's judgment and victory senses remain live.

epistemic.reason: The coordinates match supplied Arabic anchors, while four context roots remain unresolved and their roles are preserved as HFT attribution.

Two retrospective supports name 32:30 without supplying its Arabic surface or a trace coordinate. Both findings were narrowed to 32:29; no claim about the exact wording of 32:30 is carried.

The o01 HFT path maps the exact q-l-l token at 32:9 word 12 through root_001251, whose registry root label is q-w-l while B001's smallness source image is q-l-l. The connected instability remains attributed and exploratory.
The 54:11 connection carries reciprocal no-value evidence for the reverse direction. Its exact opened-gates/water surface is retained only as a bounded focus-directed water analogy.

The 4:4 reciprocal counterevidence concerns bridal dues and limits any transfer of that usage onto ṣādiqīn; the costly-transfer reading uses the distinct 32:16 provision/expenditure trigger and stays exploratory.
